title: Strong Fairness — weak vs strong decision rule, eight assumptions; 'fairness gives work its chance, progress proves the chance accomplished something'

source.source_reference: Shawn's explicit teaching, main chat, 2026-10-10. Filed same-evening per his standing law: his word IS the verification (Verification Law); filed immediately, not queued.

intelligence.essence: Weak fairness says: if work is CONTINUOUSLY eligible, it eventually gets served. Strong fairness says: if work is eligible INFINITELY OFTEN — even with gaps — it eventually gets served. The difference is everything for intermittent work: under weak fairness, a scheduler can starve a task forever by letting it flicker in and out of eligibility, and the letter of the guarantee is satisfied. The eight-situation decision rule tells you exactly which standard applies where; the eight-assumption checklist must be satisfied before a strong-fairness claim is made. The flicker ledger tracks eligibility oscillation so the 'it wasn't continuously eligible' defense can be audited. The decisive experiment: two schedulers, one weak-fair one strong-fair, on the same flickering workload — only the strong-fair one serves the intermittent task.

human_view.meaning: Weak fairness protects work that's always ready. Strong fairness protects work that keeps becoming ready, over and over, with gaps. Without strong fairness, a scheduler can starve intermittent work forever while technically keeping its promise.
human_view.why_it_matters: Intermittent eligibility is the normal case in real systems (resources come and go). Weak fairness alone legalizes starvation of exactly the work that needs protection.

simple_view.meaning: Weak fairness protects work that's always ready. Strong fairness protects work that keeps becoming ready, over and over, with gaps. Without strong fairness, a scheduler can starve intermittent work forever while technically keeping its promise.

naya_view.directive: Apply the eight-situation decision rule to choose the standard. Satisfy the eight-assumption checklist before claiming strong fairness. Keep the flicker ledger on intermittent obligations. Never accept 'not continuously eligible' as a defense without the ledger.

ai_view.specification: WF: □eligible → ◇served. SF: □◇eligible → ◇served. Decision rule: 8 situations → standard. Checklist: 8 assumptions. Flicker ledger records eligibility oscillation.
ai_view.directive: Follow as written. This is law, not guidance.
